sectorSummary.overview: Loan books and secured lending expanded across the seven banks, with stronger operating earnings at several franchises. The recovery remains uneven: Utkarsh is loss-making, guarantee receipts and write-offs affect reported asset quality, and funding costs, succession and weather risks qualify the outlook.

trends.text: Banks continue to diversify toward secured lending and more individual or retail products while growing loan books.
Retail deposits and deeper customer relationships remain central to funding growth.

tailwinds.text: Improving collections and lower incremental credit stress support earnings recovery, although reported ratios can also benefit from write-offs, guarantees or asset sales.

headwinds.text: Competition for deposits and repricing of liabilities keep funding costs and margins under pressure.
Drought and other weather disruptions require close monitoring of borrower cash flows and collections.

opportunities.text: Capital’s expansion outside Punjab and ESAF’s technology upgrade offer routes to wider distribution and better productivity.
Ujjivan and Suryoday are expanding product reach while seeking better productivity from their lending and deposit platforms.

risks.text: Fresh CGFMU guarantees are not yet open; Jana, Suryoday and Utkarsh rely on reopening or future cover despite accruing fees.
Equitas and Ujjivan are managing CEO succession, with regulatory selection and approval still ahead.
Utkarsh’s continuing loss and Suryoday’s lower exit ROA objective show that the recovery is not uniform.

insights.text: Credit-cost denominators differ: Equitas quotes average gross advances, while Ujjivan uses average total assets; direct ratio comparisons can mislead.
Guarantee claims, legacy write-offs and asset-sale effects need to be separated from underlying collection improvement.
